chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a merchant who traded with capital and stipulated half the profit: 'There is no guarantee/liability on the Mudarib (worker).' And he also said: 'Whoever guarantees the profit for his Mudarib, he is entitled only to the principal capital and he gets nothing from the profit.'

key_terms.رَأْسُ الْمَالِ: The principal capital contributed by the investor
key_terms.مُضَارِب: The worker or partner who contributes labor in a Mudarabah partnership

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on profit-sharing in Mudarabah if the worker is not liable for loss?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites the judicial precedent of Imam Ali (AS) to clarify that in a Mudarabah contract, the absence of liability for loss on the worker (Mudarib) is a defining feature; however, if the capital owner guarantees the profit, the worker forfeits their share, retaining only the principal. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between true partnership and interest-based loans, ensuring that risk-sharing remains integral to the validity of the profit-sharing arrangement.
